_comment: Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/LiquationFurnace/tools/make_shape.py. Native frame, block units, controller cell at [0,0,0]: the front west cell at ground level, where the niche is. A tin-lead liquation furnace (#929): an iron hearth plate falling to the front under a low vault open at the front, over a fire; its low end spouts into the receiving pot in the niche under it. Worked from the front (plate: the cakes put on and the lead taken off; pot: the tin taken out) and fired from the back (fireDoor; ash, the damper). Furnaces stand side by side in a row along x (up to furnace.rowMax), sharing one chimney on one member's outlet, the others capped. No power and no forced air: natural draught, in at the ash mouth under the damper and at the working opening, out at the outlet. depth is the fire door: 0 open, slid up in its guides (the rest pose), 1 shut over the fire hole. theta is the stoker's clock, carried by a ratio-0 rotate on the door: nothing turns. requires: the build's stages, brickwork, lining and fittings (build; the fittings are the parts plate, pot and door; the frame, iron, has none); cakes, tinrun, tin and lead (the charge); fuel1, fuel2 (the fuel's two layers from the grate up) and the same burning, fire1, fire2; the damper's place, damperopen, damperhalf or dampershut (one at a time); and outletcap. The brickwork's texture is the furnace's brick type's (bricks). outletCell: the stack's top, in the back row's east cell (a chimney stands on one cell), the chimney stood on its top; chimney: the shortest chimney, counted from the outlet up. See LiquationFurnace/README.md.

build._comment: The build's stages, in order. frame: the iron frame's grid recipe (with a hammer); placing it puts down the controller and its ghosts, and draws the frame part. Each stage then fits its requires when its materials are all in: brickwork, then lining (the vault with it), then fittings (parts: the hearth plate with its spout, the receiving pot and the fire door; also: the damper, in one of its places). volumeBlocks: the stage's brick measured from the model, in blocks; its quantities are that at 2 fired bricks or 4 refractory bricks a block (the game's brick block recipes), rounded up, fire clay one per 2.5 refractory bricks. perClick stack: a click puts in as many of the held stack as are still needed. oneType: the first fired brick put in sets the furnace's brick type (bricks), and the rest must match. The frame's recipe and the fittings' materials are proposals (LiquationFurnace/README.md). outletCap: an item interaction, not a stage. The contents and the damper are drawn once the fittings are in, the cap once the lining is.

bricks._comment: The fired brick types the brickwork takes (every game:burnedbrick type), each with the block its bricks make and that block's texture: the renderer sets the shape's 'brick' code to the furnace's type's base, with its overlays drawn over it. The furnace's type is the first brick put in; until then no brick is drawn. A type missing here (another mod's) is refused. The crucible furnace's list (cruciblefurnace-rig.json).

furnace._comment: fuelLayers: the fuel on the grate is drawn as its layers fuel1.. (fire.. while lit), how much a layer holds is gameplay's; cakes: the cakes drawn on the plate; minChimney: chimney blocks stood on the outlet, counted from it up; rowMax, rowAxis: furnaces in a row, side by side along x, sharing one chimney; doorTravel: how far the fire door slides (blocks, the door's step); plateSlope: the hearth plate's fall to the front, rise per run.
